# Design

Three waves. Wave 1 builds six foundations that share no file, so six lanes run at once: the EVM vault moves to bridge/evm and is hardened without moving its wire format; the Solana program's custody core - ownership, the attestor set, the asset registry, the caps, the pause, the deposit and its receipt - is written; the Solana identity mapping is documented and pinned as vectors proven against the chain's own preimage builders; the nine chain configurations, their schema and their validator are written together with the per-chain deploy and verify scripts; the governance proposal generator and the attestor-set manifest are written against the same schema; and the one CI workflow is added. Wave 2 integrates them: the Solana release path verifies attestations through the native secp256k1 program, the relayer learns to observe Solana deposits and then to submit Solana releases, the post-deploy checklist reads the chain back and compares it with the configuration, the per-chain pages and the operator runbook are written, and the two deploy dry runs are recorded against anvil and solana-test-validator. Wave 3 runs the workflow's command set once on the merged revision and writes down what ran. Two things are deliberately absent and stay absent: wrapped PAX on a foreign chain and Sidiora on the EVM mainnets are both governed upgrades for after the halt, because each needs a chain change the halt forbids.

## Identity and digests

There is one attestation contract and every destination speaks it. An attestor signs keccak256 of a packed preimage - the inbound one for a foreign deposit, the outbound one for a Paxeer burn - with secp256k1, and hands over 65 bytes of r, s and v. The EVM vault recovers those signatures with ecrecover; the Paxeer precompile recovers them in the keeper; the Solana program has them recovered for it by the native secp256k1 program. Nothing in this feature adds a second signature format, a second domain or a second hash.

Solana keys are 32 bytes and the digests carry 20, so Solana identities enter through a handle: the last 20 bytes of keccak256 of the key. The vault handle is the handle of the vault-authority PDA and is what governance registers as Solana's vault on Paxeer. An asset's 20 bytes come from the program's registry, whose default for a mint is the handle of the mint and whose owner may instead record an explicit id. A recipient's 20 bytes are derived by the program from the full 32-byte pubkey the release names, so the release can pay only the key the attestors signed for. An inbound txHash is keccak256 of the 64-byte transaction signature and an inbound logIndex is the deposit nonce the receipt PDA records.

Solana's chain id on the Paxeer side is the reserved uint64 91600046870081: the ASCII bytes of SOLANA, left-padded to eight bytes and read big-endian, 0x0000534f4c414e41. It is orders of magnitude above every EIP-155 id in use, so it can never collide with one, and governance registers it through MsgRegisterChain like any other chain.

Sidiora's Solana mint is registered with the explicit asset id 0x21f7b20a555199fa73A238B1a91FD0f549068fEe rather than its derived handle, because the chain has already fixed that pair: EnsureSidioraDenom registers the bridged asset (chain id, that address, usid), so an inbound SID deposit resolves to the denom the bridge module already administers and no alias is needed. The binding is exclusive both ways: the id 0x21f7b20a555199fa73A238B1a91FD0f549068fEe is accepted only for the mint 5w3wVdJaESaJKyLmStM6Hv9UyUkmZ1b9DLQquAqqpump, and that mint only with that id, and anything else is refused by the Solana program's asset registration, by the configuration validator and by the post-deploy checklist.

bridge/ATTESTATION-SOLANA.md states all of this with a worked example, and bridge/vectors pins it: the handle of the Sidiora mint against the asset id 0x21f7b20a555199fa73A238B1a91FD0f549068fEe, the handle of the vault-authority PDA, the handle of the wrapped SOL mint, and a full inbound and outbound digest for a Sidiora transfer. The vectors are recomputed in Go against modules/layerxbridge/types.InboundPreimage and OutboundPreimage - the chain's own builders, read and not edited - and asserted again by the Solana program's tests and the relayer's tests, so the three implementations cannot drift.

## Where the code lives

bridge/evm is interop/contracts/ethereum-bridge moved with git mv, so PaxeerXVault.sol, BridgeAttestation.sol, their tests and ATTESTATION.md keep their history. It gains script for the Foundry deploy script, chains for the eight EVM configurations and their pages, lib for the two pinned libraries and bootstrap-libs.sh to fetch them. Its foundry.toml keeps solc 0.8.30, the optimizer at 100000 runs, via_ir, no bytecode hash and no metadata, so the bytecode is reproducible, and writes its artifacts under build.

bridge/solana is a self-contained crate with its own workspace and lockfile, laid out like interop/contracts/solana-mirror: src/lib.rs with the entrypoint and the instruction dispatch, one module per concern, tests under tests driven by solana-program-test, and chains/solana holding the Solana configuration and its page.

bridge/deploy holds the parts that are neither contract nor program: chainconfig, the Go package that defines the configuration schema, loads it and refuses a placeholder; proposals, the Go package and command that emit the governance messages; the attestor-set manifest; deploy-evm-chain.sh, verify-evm-chain.sh and deploy-solana-program.sh; checklist.sh, which reads the deployed state back and compares it with the configuration; and tests, the offline check scripts that exercise every script the way interop/deploy/mirror/tests exercises the mirror's.

bridge/vectors is a small Go package holding the shared identity and digest vectors and the handle derivation, with the test that proves them against the chain's preimage builders. bridge/README.md is the operator runbook: what to deploy, in what order, with which environment variables, which proposals to submit, and what the checklist must report before the bridge is opened.

## The chains and their configuration

Eight EVM chains and Solana. The EVM chains are ethereum (1), base (8453), arbitrum (42161), optimism (10), bnb (56), polygon (137), avalanche (43114) and hyperevm (999, Hyperliquid). Solana is the reserved id 91600046870081. Every EVM chain gets identical bytecode from one source; hyperevm gets one extra sentence in its page and one flag in its configuration, because a contract deployment there needs the account switched to big blocks first and will otherwise run out of block gas.

One JSON schema serves all nine. A configuration names the chain, its numeric id, the native coin's symbol and decimals, the environment variable holding the RPC endpoint, the environment variable holding the explorer verification key, the owner address, the attestor addresses and the threshold, the finality depth, and the asset list. The first asset of every chain is its native coin - address(0) on an EVM chain with eighteen decimals, the wrapped SOL mint on Solana with nine - and it is always registered, so the default pair PAX against the chain's native coin works the moment the chain is opened. Each asset carries its address or mint, its 20-byte asset id, its decimals, its per-transaction cap and its total cap.

The validator in bridge/deploy/chainconfig is what makes the configuration trustworthy: it refuses an unknown field, a chain id that is not the one the file's name claims, a native symbol or decimals that do not match the chain, an environment variable name that is empty or not upper snake case, a placeholder or zero owner, a placeholder, zero, duplicated or out-of-order attestor, a threshold of zero or above the attestor count, a finality depth of zero, an asset list whose first entry is not the native coin, a cap of zero, and a Solana asset id that does not match either the mint's derived handle or, for Sidiora, 0x21f7b20a555199fa73A238B1a91FD0f549068fEe. Every refusal names the file and the field. The chainconfig package task 1.4 writes is the single configuration schema of the bridge: the proposals generator of task 1.5 imports it rather than declaring a schema of its own, and the handle derivation lives only in bridge/vectors.

The per-chain pages name the pair in plain words - PAX against ETH on ethereum, base, arbitrum and optimism, against BNB on bnb, POL on polygon, AVAX on avalanche, HYPE on hyperevm and SOL on solana - and say what the operator must have in hand before running the deploy script.

## The Solana program

One program holds custody for Solana. A config PDA holds the owner, the pending owner of a two-step transfer, the paused flag, the attestor set as up to 64 twenty-byte addresses with the threshold, the deposit nonce and the bumps. A vault-authority PDA signs for the program's token accounts and is the identity whose handle Paxeer registers as Solana's vault. An asset PDA per mint records the mint, the 20-byte asset id, the decimals, the per-transaction cap, the total cap, the amount outstanding and whether it is enabled. A deposit-receipt PDA per nonce records the deposit, which is what makes the nonce monotonic and auditable. A nullifier PDA per (paxeerTxHash, paxeerNonce) is created by a release, so a replayed release fails because the account already exists.

A deposit moves SPL tokens by CPI from the depositor's token account into the vault's, admits the amount against the asset's caps, refuses a zero amount, refuses a recipient whose high twelve bytes are not zero or whose low twenty bytes are zero, increments the nonce, writes the receipt and logs the record the relayer reads. The program never learns its own transaction signature and does not need to: the relayer computes the inbound txHash as keccak256 of the signature it observed, and reads the nonce from the receipt.

A release verifies the same outbound digest every other destination verifies, without carrying elliptic-curve code. The program rebuilds the 185-byte outbound preimage from the Solana chain id, the vault handle, the paxeerTxHash and paxeerNonce, the handle of the 32-byte recipient the instruction names, the asset id from the registry and the amount; it then reads the instructions sysvar, finds the native secp256k1 program's instruction in the same transaction, and requires that it carries at least threshold signature entries, that every entry's message bytes are exactly that preimage, that every entry's offsets resolve inside the secp256k1 instruction's own data, that every 64-byte signature has s at or below half the curve order, and that the recovered ethereum addresses are current attestors in strictly ascending order with no repeat. The native program having already verified each signature over keccak256 of the message, an accepted release is one the same attestors could have released on any EVM chain. Anything unresolved, out of order, unknown or short of the threshold refuses.

Then the release creates the nullifier PDA, reduces the asset's outstanding amount, moves the tokens out by CPI and logs the record. Every instruction is refused while the program is paused except the owner's unpause, and every owner instruction is refused for any other signer.

Paxeer's bridgeOut carries a 20-byte recipient, so the relayer cannot recover a 32-byte Solana pubkey from it; a permissionless recipient registry closes that gap. A Solana account registers its own pubkey under its 20-byte handle in a recipient PDA seeded by the handle, signing for that pubkey, and the program verifies that the last 20 bytes of keccak256 of the pubkey equal the handle before writing the PDA, which is never overwritten. The relayer reads that PDA before submitting a release and holds the release in its journal as pending-recipient until the PDA exists, so an outbound transfer to an unregistered handle waits rather than fails or guesses.

## The relayer's Solana side

The relayer keeps one shape and gains one chain. The configuration grows a solana entry carrying what a chains[] entry carries - the chain id, the vault handle, the finality depth in slots, the start slot, the maximum slot range, the RPC quorum and the fee-payer key handle - plus the program id and the commitment. The fee-payer handle names an ed25519 key the remote signer holds; no key material enters the configuration, and the validator refuses a solana entry whose fee-payer handle is the attestor handle.

The observer follows the program with getSlot and getSignaturesForAddress, reads each transaction with getTransaction, keeps the deposits confirmed to the configured slot depth, computes the inbound attestation from the deposit record and the receipt PDA read with getAccountInfo, signs it with the existing secp256k1 attestor key and submits bridgeIn to the precompile through the Paxeer link that already exists. The journal keys it under the same inbound stream shape the EVM chains use, so exactly-once submission and restart behaviour are the ones already proven.

The submitter watches BridgeOut on Paxeer as it already does, builds the release instruction with the recipient's full pubkey, prepends the native secp256k1 instruction carrying the threshold signatures over the outbound preimage, fetches a blockhash with getLatestBlockhash, has the fee payer sign the message under the policy domain LayerX/bridge/solana-tx/v1, journals the signed bytes before broadcast, sends it with sendTransaction and confirms it with getSignatureStatuses. A nullifier PDA that already exists is a completed submission, not an error to retry.

Both loops are proven by recorded fixtures in the existing format, with a real signer socket and a real journal on disk, so no production path is faked.

## Deployment, governance and the checklist

Deployment is one script per kind of chain and one order. deploy-evm-chain.sh takes a chain name, loads and validates its configuration, refuses every placeholder, builds with the pinned libraries, deploys the vault with the Foundry script, sets the attestor set and the caps the configuration names, reads the deployed code back and writes a deployment record naming the chain, the address, the deployer, the code hash and the block. verify-evm-chain.sh submits the source to the chain's explorer through the key its configuration names. deploy-solana-program.sh builds with cargo-build-sbf and deploys with the pinned Solana toolchain, in the shape interop/deploy/mirror/deploy-solana-mirror.sh already uses, then initialises the program and registers the assets the configuration names.

Governance comes next and is generated, not typed. The proposals command reads a chain configuration and emits, as JSON bodies matching the module's own message types field for field, MsgRegisterChain for the chain and its vault handle, MsgSetAttestors for the shared attestor set and threshold, and one MsgSetCap per asset - always including the native coin, and for Solana including the usid cap for Sidiora. The generator marshals the real types from modules/layerxbridge/types, which it imports and does not modify, so a body cannot drift from what the keeper will accept, and its test decodes every body back into those types with unknown fields forbidden and runs their ValidateBasic.

The attestor-set manifest is the one place the attestor addresses and the threshold are written down, and every chain configuration is checked against it, so a chain cannot be brought up with a different set by accident. It carries addresses and a threshold only: no key material, no endpoint and no operator identity.

checklist.sh is the gate before the bridge is opened. For each chain it reads the deployed state back through the chain's own RPC - the vault's owner, attestors and threshold, the per-asset caps, the paused flag, the deployed code hash on an EVM chain and the program's config and asset PDAs on Solana - and reads the Paxeer side back through the precompile's views, then compares every value with the configuration and the generated proposals and reports one line per check. The native coin is checked first, and any mismatch, any placeholder and any missing registration fails the run.
